# Topic A — Samples, Populations & Bias


## Q1 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Compare a simple random sample of 60 fish with the true population mean.

```{r q1-data, eval=TRUE}
set.seed(2026)
pop <- round(rnorm(10000, mean = 0.9, sd = 0.3), 2)   # mercury (ppm) of 10,000 fish
```

```{r q1-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
mu <- mean(pop)                         # population parameter (normally unknown)
set.seed(1)
srs <- sample(pop, size = 60)           # simple random sample, without replacement
xbar <- mean(srs)                       # sample statistic
round(c(mu = mu, xbar = xbar, error = xbar - mu), 4)
```

## Q5 · L5 · Scenario 2

**Goal:** A university emails 2,000 students; only 30% reply, and students who reply study more hours. Simulate this and show how non-response biases the estimate of mean study hours. Write a 3-sentence report.

```{r q5-data, eval=TRUE}
set.seed(55)
hours <- round(rgamma(2000, shape = 4, rate = 0.25), 1)      # weekly study hours of all students
p_reply <- pmin(0.9, 0.05 + hours / 40)                     # keener students reply more often
replied <- runif(2000) < p_reply
```

```{r q5-l5}
# 1. True mean hours of all 2,000 students
# 2. Response rate
# 3. Mean hours of the students who replied
# 4. Size of the bias
# 5. Report (3 sentences as comments):
```

# Topic B — Test Statistics & p-values


## Q6 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** A machine should fill 500 g bags (σ = 6 g). A sample of 36 bags has mean 502.5 g. Test H0: μ = 500 vs Ha: μ ≠ 500.

```{r q6-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
xbar <- 502.5; mu0 <- 500; sigma <- 6; n <- 36
se <- sigma / sqrt(n)
z <- (xbar - mu0) / se                     # test statistic = standardized score
p_two <- 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE)
round(c(se = se, z = z, p = p_two), 4)
if (p_two < 0.05) cat("Reject H0\n") else cat("Fail to reject H0\n")
```

# Topic C — Errors, Power & Effect Size


## Q11 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** If H0 is true and we test at α = 0.05, how often do we wrongly reject?

```{r q11-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
set.seed(11)
p_values <- replicate(5000, {
  x <- rnorm(30, mean = 50, sd = 10)          # H0 (mu = 50) is TRUE
  t.test(x, mu = 50)$p.value
})
type1_rate <- mean(p_values < 0.05)
type1_rate                                    # close to alpha = 0.05
```

# Topic D — Standard Error & Confidence Intervals


## Q16 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Sample means of a right-skewed variable become approximately normal as n grows.

```{r q16-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
set.seed(16)
skewed <- rexp(100000, rate = 1 / 20)          # right-skewed population, mean 20, sd 20
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(skewed, breaks = 60, main = "Population", col = "gray")
means40 <- replicate(2000, mean(sample(skewed, 40)))
hist(means40, breaks = 40, main = "Means of n = 40", col = "lightblue")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
se_theory <- sd(skewed) / sqrt(40)
round(c(sd_of_means = sd(means40), se_theory = se_theory), 3)
```
